subject: GalaxyCare: priority-lane saturation causing morning p95 and 5xx — urgent triage
messages:
From: Emily Wong <emily.wong@galaxycare.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: ops@galaxycare.com
Date: 2026-12-08T09:03:12-05:00
Subject: Morning peak: p95 spike and 502s — urgent

Naomi,

We started seeing sustained p95 latency spike (~1.8s -> 4.6s) and intermittent 502/503 errors across our API between 08:45–09:00 ET this morning. Error rate peaked at ~3.2% for a 10m window. This is impacting our customer-facing search autocomplete; several enterprise customers reported degraded UX.

Attached is a short CSV export from our front-end relay (perf_spike_1208.csv) showing the spike window and request IDs. We haven't made any config changes on our side today.

Can you triage and tell us whether this looks like something on Redwood's serving side (batching/cache) or if it's on our side? We need a short update in 30m for our internal ops standup; CTO is on standby.

—Emily Wong
Sr. Ops Manager, GalaxyCare
[Attachment: perf_spike_1208.csv (CSV, 34KB)]

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-08T09:20:45-05:00
Subject: Fwd: Morning peak: p95 spike and 502s — urgent

Team — forwarding an urgent customer report (GalaxyCare). Emily attached a CSV. CTO is already looped on their side; they want a 30m status. Quick ask: can someone validate whether this matches recent priority-lane saturation symptoms (HOL blocking, KV partitions thrashing) and propose immediate mitigations we can run with low blast radius?

High level facts from Emily: p95 jumped to ~4.6s, 5xxs briefly ~3.2% peak, no config change on their side.

Please reply-all with the triage and a short mitigation plan. If we need an exec call, I'll coordinate with GalaxyCare.

—Naomi
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-08T09:35:10-05:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Morning peak: p95 spike and 502s — urgent

Naomi / team — initial read: this pattern smells like priority-lane saturation + KV cache thrash. Key indicators: high p95 with transient 5xxs during the same window, and no upstream config changes. I pulled recent metrics (KV eviction rate rose sharply at 08:42, prefetch queue depth spiked).

Immediate mitigations to propose (low-risk, reversible):
- Decrease priority-lane weight for the suspect tenant by 30% (reduces HOL blocking across lanes).
- Enable per-tenant cache partitioning for their tenant id to limit noisy-neighbor eviction (runtime flag).
- Temporarily reduce max_batch_size for that tenant to cap per-request memory and reduce KV pressure.
- If errors persist, fall back their routing policy to a slightly higher-latency but less-loaded model variant for 15 minutes (auto-fallback).

I'll prepare the runbook steps and console commands. If we have ops approval, I can run the changes in 10m.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-08T10:10:02-05:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Morning peak: p95 spike and 502s — urgent

Adding details from the runtime side and a small log excerpt. I pulled the kv / prefetch stats for tenant GC-4721: eviction spikes at 08:41:58, hot-lane queue depth grew from median 12 -> 86, and we observed repeated prefix collisions on the tenant's hot shards. That combination causes HOL blocking for other batches hitting the same worker.

Log excerpt: 
[2026-12-08T08:41:58Z] tenant=GC-4721 kv_eviction=374 prefetch_q=86 batch_wait_ms=1200
[2026-12-08T08:42:05Z] tenant=GC-4721 hot_lane_hold=4 prefetch_hit_ratio=0.12

Proposed concrete steps (runbook attached):
1) Apply per-tenant cache partitioning flag: runtime toggle -> partition_count=8 for tenant GC-4721.
2) Reduce priority-lane_weight for tenant by 0.7 -> 0.5.
3) Rolling restart of 4 workers serving hot-lane to reclaim fragmented KV segments (staggered, 30s drain).
4) Observe for 10m; if p95 remains >2.0s, enable fallback routing to model-variant-small for traffic matching their priority queue.

I attached kv_stats_1208.log and mitigation_runbook_1208.md with exact console commands. These changes are reversible and low-risk; rolling restarts are the only disruptive step and we will do them one node at a time.

[Attachment: kv_stats_1208.log (TXT, 78KB)]
[Attachment: mitigation_runbook_1208.md (MD, 4KB)]

—Marissa
Principal Reliability Engineer — Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-12-08T10:20:30-05:00
Subject: Re: Morning peak: p95 spike and 502s — urgent

Emily — thank you for the heads-up and the CSV. We're treating this as an incident and have a small ops runbook ready. Immediate plan (summary for your CTO and ops):
- We're going to enable per-tenant cache partitioning for GC-4721 and reduce their priority-lane weight. This limits eviction bleed and reduces head-of-line blocking risk.
- We'll do a rolling restart of a few hot-lane workers to reclaim fragmented memory; restarts are staggered to avoid service disruption.
- We will monitor p95, 5xx rate and KV eviction rate; aim to have an initial stabilization within 30–45 minutes.

I propose a short sync at 11:00 ET to confirm customer-visible impact and next steps. Please confirm if that works for your team. We'll share dashboards and the runbook link during the call.

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Emily Wong <emily.wong@galaxycare.com>, ops@galaxycare.com
Date: 2026-12-08T11:45:22-05:00
Subject: Incident update: stabilization observed after mitigations

Quick update after changes (applied at ~11:05 ET):
- Per-tenant cache partitioning enabled (partition_count=8 for GC-4721).
- Priority-lane weight reduced to 0.5 for GC-4721.
- Rolling restart of 4 hot-lane workers completed (one-by-one).

Preliminary impact (rolling window 11:05–11:40 ET):
- p95 latency reduced from 4.6s -> 1.9s (customer-side telemetry and our Grafana p95).
- 5xx rate dropped from 3.2% peak -> <0.2%.
- KV eviction rate normalized to baseline.

Next steps:
- Keep the config changes for 2 hours and re-evaluate; if stable, we'll make per-tenant partitioning the default for tenants with observed hot-shard patterns.
- Marissa will follow up with a post-incident write-up and recommended long-term changes (adaptive lane-weighting, more aggressive prefetch TTL heuristics).

Emily / GalaxyCare — please let us know if you're seeing the same stabilization on your side. We'll keep monitoring and share the post-mortem by EOD.

—Jonas
SRE Lead, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference
